newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate rises to 8.7 pct in thin market.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate rises to 8.7 pct in thin market.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate rose to 8.7 percent from 7.0/7.5 percent on Friday as market liquidity appeared to be still tight, dealers said.
The overnight was traded from a low of 8.0 percent.
Dealers said Monday's trading was thin with few players seen in the market.
"It's very quiet today with Bank Negara heard capping the overnight at 8.7 percent," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
"The market is still tight but I think rates should consolidate. The question now is how fast Bank Negara wants rates to come off," he said.
Agent banks of Bank Negara Malaysia were seen lending overnight funds from 10 percent to 7.5 percent on Friday, dealers said.
Earlier, one-month money was at 9.0/9.3 percent against 10.0 percent on Friday. The three-month rate was at 8.0/9.0 percent against 9.5 percent.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange stayed firm on the back of softening interbank rates on the cash market.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up two points to 92.43, or an implied yield of 7.57 percent.
The March 1998 contract was up one to 92.74, or 7.26 percent.
